title: The School Funding Story Almost Everyone's Missing
author: Alexander Russo
summary: Alexander Russo argues that press and public coverage of the incoming Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program has fixated almost entirely on its potential to fund private-school vouchers while missing that the same law, through a late drafting change, also opens a significant new revenue stream for public schools. Citing Edunomics Lab estimates of roughly $1,000 per public-school student annually, Russo frames this as consequential news for districts currently squeezed by expiring COVID relief funds and declining enrollment, arriving via a confusing mechanism where taxpayers direct $1,700 to intermediary "scholarship granting organizations" that public schools must then craft allowable fees to collect against. He contrasts the thin coverage of this story with the outsized media attention paid to canceled mental-health grants affecting under 2 percent of districts, arguing the mismatch in attention is striking given the tax-credit program's far larger potential per-pupil impact across every district.
points: Reveals that the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program, widely covered only as a private-school voucher mechanism, was changed in final drafting to also direct funds toward public schools, an angle largely missing from coverage.

Cites Edunomics Lab's estimate that the program could generate roughly $1,000 annually per public school student, arriving as many districts face budget gaps from expiring COVID relief funds and declining enrollment.

Explains the mechanism's complexity: taxpayers direct $1,700 to intermediary scholarship-granting organizations, and public schools must craft an 'allowable fee' structure to collect against that money.
Contrasts thin coverage of this program (affecting every district, worth potentially 100 times more per pupil) with heavy coverage of canceled mental-health grants affecting under 2% of districts.
quotes: What most people don't seem to understand yet is that there's a lot of money on the table for public schools. Yes, public schools.

Edunomics Lab estimates that the program could ultimately generate $1,000 annually per public school student. That's good news at a time when many districts face budget gaps resulting from expiring COVID relief funds and declining enrollment.
The currently signed law-of-the-land is a program whereby each taxpayer can direct $1,700 of their federal taxes to support students who attend private OR PUBLIC schools.
Compare this story to the widespread coverage of canceled mental health grants, grant sums that go to less than 2% of districts and amount to less than $10 per K-12 student.
I think it is fair to say that tax credit scholarships have received a fraction of that attention despite the potential to impact every district and generate 100X that per pupil.
